correctness.rationale: For all q>=3 positive integer arm lengths, the polar of the edge-molecule crosspolytope is a cube of signed edge potentials. The pairwise variance identity along an arm yields (L+1)(u-v)>=w²-s²; changing a nonmonotone signed arm to a ramp gives strict gain at least (w²-s²)(1/(L+1)-1/N)>0. Thus extremizing potentials must use constant gradients per arm. Their normalized squared norm is sum u_i - delta²/N with triangular signed weights w_i. Center symmetry makes this global inradius, maximizers count |E|, and independent arm depth vectors give center-locus rank n-rank(E). Own exhaustive signed-edge test of (1,2,3,4), (1,1,2,3), (2,2,2) matches exact norm and contact count; finite only. The printed occurrence of nu_i in the theorem is an obvious undefined symbol for its explicitly defined u_i; the proof and example unambiguously specify sum u_i. It is a minor notational defect, not the reason for rejection.
